newsitem.title: CANADA: Mobil studying Canada oil sands project.
newsitem.headline: Mobil studying Canada oil sands project.

text.p: Mobil Corp unit Mobil Oil Canada said on Friday it informed regulators about its plans for a proposed oil sands mining and bitumen extraction project in Alberta's Athabasca region.
Mobil said it planned to study the feasability of developing an open-pit mine designed to produce 100,000 barrels per day of bitumen with production starting in 2003.
The company, saying that plans were in the early stages, estimated recoverable bitumen reserves on its wholly owned Lease #36, 70 km north of Fort McMurray, Alberta, at 1.2 to 1.4 billion barrels.

Mobil officials declined to estimate the eventual costs of building the project, although a similar-sized oil sands operation proposed recently by Shell Canada Ltd was estimated to have a price tag of about C$1 billion.

"We're working to confirm the necessary technical and economic data to make a business decision whther to proceed with the project within the next two years," Mobil Canada vice-president Wayne Kubasek said in a statement.
Under current plans, Mobil would submit a Development Plan Apllication in Mid-1998 and start construction by the year 2000.
The company said it anticipated using truck-and-shovel technology to mine the ore body and was considering moving the bitumen through one of several pipelines currently being planned in the region.
